classification.difficultyReason: Interpret equally spaced lake widths, including zero endpoint widths, and apply the composite trapezoidal rule.

content.prompt: The diagram shows the width of a lake at 10-metre intervals. Use the trapezoidal rule to estimate the surface area of the water.

spec.description: Irregular lake outline with solid internal width measurements and dashed guides to five equally spaced position labels. The endpoints have zero width; no endpoint-width numbers or separate axis are printed.
spec.answerVisibility: All diagram content is supplied in the student question.

answer.worked:
The interval spacing is $h=10\text{ m}$. The widths at positions $0,10,20,30,40\text{ m}$ are $0,20,18,17,0\text{ m}$.
$$\begin{aligned}A&\approx\frac{10}{2}\bigl[0+2(20)+2(18)+2(17)+0\bigr]\\&=5(110)\\&=550\text{ m}^2.\end{aligned}$$
